title: Repeatable and reproducible research
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T09:32:52Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The bank point on ethical research covers informed consent, confidentiality, avoiding harm and respect, which is a different idea from the new point's concern with whether a finding can be repeated and reproduced, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Repeatable and reproducible research
card: The same researchers run the same study again, using the same methods, and get a similar result.
Other researchers run the study using the same methods with new participants, and get a similar result.
A single result might come from chance or from an unusual group of participants. Getting the result again makes it less likely to be a fluke.
A finding is stronger when it is both repeated and reproduced. If it cannot be, doubt about the finding grows.
draft.remember: Getting the same result again, by the same team or a new one, makes a finding stronger.

a.q: A team in Perth runs a memory experiment and later runs it again themselves with the same methods. What have they tested?
opts: Whether the finding is repeatable
Whether the finding is reproducible
Whether the finding is an opinion
Whether the finding is secondary data
a.why: The same researchers repeated their own study, so this tests repeatability. Reproducibility needs other researchers and new participants, which is why that option is wrong.

b.q: A lab in Brisbane finds that a breathing exercise lowers stress. A team in Hobart runs the same method with new participants and gets a similar result. What does this show?
opts: The finding is reproducible, so it is stronger
The finding is repeatable, so it is stronger
The finding is proven true for every person
The finding is weaker because different people took part
b.why: Another team used the same methods with new participants and got a similar result, so the finding is reproducible. It is not repeatable in this sense, since the original team did not run it again. Reproduction makes it stronger but does not prove it for everyone.
b.clue: Think about who ran the second study and who took part.

b.best: The finding is reproducible, so it is stronger

problems.detail: The card defines reproducible as other researchers using 'the same methods'. The VCE Study Design glossary defines reproducibility as agreement of results under changed conditions, such as a different operator, location, instrument or method. The card's definition is narrower than the syllabus one and could mislead students in assessment. Consider 'Other researchers run the study again, often with new participants and sometimes in a different way, and get a similar result.'

check.summary: Both questions are sound and each has one clear answer. The card's definition of 'reproducible' requires the same methods, which is narrower than the VCE glossary, where reproducibility allows changed conditions including a different method.
